title: Sectoral AI Governance Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Sectoral AI Governance Act of 2026 is a law that establishes specific rules and oversight for artificial intelligence technologies within key industry sectors. It aims to ensure AI is used safely, ethically, and transparently in fields such as finance, healthcare, and transportation, while providing mechanisms for accountability and compliance.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 seeks to curb the practice of artificially inflating the costs of AI services. It also aims to prevent companies from using AI systems to manipulate employee wages.

title: American AI Security Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The American AI Security Act is a U.S. law designed to set rules and standards for how artificial intelligence is developed and used so that it supports national security and public safety. It establishes responsibilities for companies, requires transparency about AI systems, and creates oversight mechanisms to monitor and manage potential risks.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that Congress must refuse to provide any additional funds or exceptional regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing insolvency or financial collapse due to exposures to acute stress within the artificial intelligence market and must provide support to all harmed Americans instead.
action: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House says Congress must not give extra money or special regulatory help to companies or banks that are in financial trouble because of stress in the artificial intelligence market. Instead, it argues that assistance should go directly to Americans who have been harmed by these problems.

title: VET Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The VET Artificial Intelligence Act is a set of rules aimed at guiding how artificial intelligence is used in vocational education and training. It seeks to protect learners, ensure fairness and transparency, and promote the safe and responsible integration of AI tools into training programs.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is a law designed to safeguard the role of human physicians in healthcare. It limits the use of artificial intelligence to assist, not replace, doctors in diagnosis and treatment, ensuring that patients are ultimately cared for by qualified medical professionals.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 would require companies that use automated decision systems to conduct risk assessments and document the impact of those systems. The law aims to promote transparency and reduce discrimination by mandating regular reviews and public disclosure of algorithmic decision‑making practices.

title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The “Securing Elections From AI Deception Act” is a proposed law that aims to protect the integrity of elections by preventing the use of artificial intelligence to spread false information or manipulate voter opinions. It would set rules and penalties to stop AI-generated content from influencing the voting process and help maintain public trust in electoral outcomes.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 sets rules to make AI systems trustworthy and safe. It requires developers to test and validate their models, share safety data, and follow standards for transparency and accountability.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: This act requires the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs to disclose any AI systems it uses, explaining how they work and who created them. It also mandates regular reporting on AI decisions that affect veterans, ensuring transparency and accountability in all VA AI applications.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act establishes rules and oversight for using AI in processing Veterans Affairs claims, ensuring that algorithms are fair, transparent, and regularly audited to prevent bias and protect veterans’ rights. The act also sets up accountability structures for developers and VA officials to correct errors and maintain trust in automated decision‑making.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is a legal framework designed to shield consumers from misleading or harmful AI products and services. It sets out rules for transparency, accountability, and consumer protection to ensure that AI systems cannot be used to deceive or manipulate users.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act is a proposed law designed to help the United States prepare for and protect against the risks associated with advanced artificial‑intelligence technologies. It would establish standards, oversight mechanisms, and coordination among agencies to monitor AI development, deployment, and security, thereby safeguarding national infrastructure and the public from potential threats.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act establishes a dedicated task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to assess and mitigate AI-related risks to critical infrastructure. It promotes collaboration with industry and other agencies to develop security guidelines, share threat intelligence, and bolster the overall resilience of AI systems.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 is a proposed law that seeks to reduce the dangers of artificial intelligence by mandating companies to evaluate and control AI risks before deploying them. It also sets standards for AI security, accountability and oversight so that developers and users can better protect people and data from harmful or unintended AI behavior.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 creates a national framework for overseeing AI technologies that directly interact with the physical world, such as robots, autonomous vehicles, and industrial machinery. It calls for collaboration among federal agencies, industry leaders, and the public to set standards for safety, security, and ethical use of these physical AI systems.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is a proposed law aimed at preventing the use of artificial intelligence to manipulate or deceive voters during elections. It seeks to establish regulations and oversight mechanisms to detect and curb AI-generated misinformation and ensure fair, transparent electoral processes.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act requires developers of AI systems that can modify their own code or improve themselves to report changes and keep detailed logs of updates. It aims to ensure transparency, safety, and accountability by allowing regulators to monitor AI evolution and prevent harmful or unintended behavior.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act proposes to curb the development and use of AI systems that could act independently and pose serious risks to people. It would establish strict rules to identify, monitor, and shut down any AI program that threatens public safety or causes significant harm.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act imposes a pause on building or running new AI data centers. The goal is to give lawmakers time to create regulations and safety standards before any new facilities are approved.
